data.name: Hacker Evolution: Untold
data.detailed_description:
When the number of computers in existence and their processing capacity exceeds that of all mankind, a point of technological singularity is encountered.
A massive economic and systematic crisis hits the entire world. Nobody knows the exact cause, and all solutions to fix it, are failing. We are about to lose our position as a dominant specie on the planet, in favor of something we have created... computers.

You play the role of Brian Spencer, a young computer programmer working for a company he started with a couple of friends, which has developed the technology from where it all started.

When you are being framed for crime, it's up to you to prevent computers from becoming the next dominant specie, and clear your name, using your hacker skills.

The concept behind Hacker Evolution: Untold is to create a game that challenges the gamers intelligence, attention and focus, creating a captivating mind game. Solve puzzles, examine code and bits of information, to help you achieve your objectives.


Key features:
  • Modding capability to allow the creation of custom levels
  • The included mod editor, allows you to create new game levels easily (PC only)
  • Complex levels and game play to guarantee the best experience
  • Complex command console with over 20 commands and tools

reviews.review:
Hacker Evolution: Untold, developed and published by exosyphen studios, takes players back to the beginnings of one of the series' central figures, Brian Spencer. Designed as a narrative prequel, the game explores the circumstances that transformed a gifted software engineer into a fugitive navigating a world of digital conspiracies. Rather than presenting hacking through realistic cybersecurity practices, the title embraces a dramatic interpretation of cyberspace where corporations, activists, and hidden organizations wage battles behind computer screens. The result is a game that feels like a love letter to early hacker fiction, combining text-driven storytelling with strategic gameplay.

The campaign is built around a succession of hacking assignments that gradually reveal a larger mystery. Players infiltrate servers, crack security systems, reroute network traffic, and retrieve sensitive information while managing limited resources. Every successful operation contributes to Brian's effort to uncover who framed him and why. The game's mission structure does a respectable job of maintaining momentum, particularly during its early hours, when new mechanics and tools are introduced at a steady pace. There is a genuine sense of progression as players gain access to stronger software and tackle increasingly complex networks.

What makes Hacker Evolution: Untold stand out is its commitment to making players think. Success is rarely achieved by clicking through menus at random. Instead, missions require observation, planning, and a willingness to experiment. Some objectives demand quick execution before tracing systems lock the player out, while others encourage a slower and more methodical approach. The combination of time pressure and strategic decision-making creates moments of tension that help sell the fantasy of operating as an elite hacker. Those who enjoy puzzle-oriented gameplay will likely appreciate the challenge, though the title's unforgiving nature can occasionally become a source of frustration.

The game's presentation reflects its independent origins and the era in which it was released. Visuals are minimalist, relying heavily on interface windows, network maps, and system readouts rather than elaborate environments. While this approach may appear dated by modern standards, it also contributes to the title's identity. The soundtrack complements the experience with atmospheric electronic tracks that reinforce the sense of isolation and urgency during critical operations. Players expecting cinematic production values will not find them here, but those willing to embrace the game's old-school sensibilities may find its simplicity surprisingly effective.

Not every aspect of the experience has aged gracefully. The user interface can be cumbersome, and tutorials often leave players to figure out important mechanics on their own. Certain missions lean too heavily on repetition, and the line between challenge and inconvenience is occasionally blurred. Additionally, the game's depiction of hacking is firmly rooted in entertainment rather than authenticity, favoring dramatic scenarios over technical realism. These shortcomings do not ruin the experience, but they do limit its appeal to a broader audience.

Even with its rough edges, Hacker Evolution: Untold remains an intriguing niche title that offers something different from conventional simulation games. Its emphasis on cyber espionage, strategic thinking, and narrative progression gives it a distinct personality that has helped the Hacker Evolution series maintain a dedicated following over the years. It is not a game for everyone, but players fascinated by computer-themed thrillers and deliberate gameplay may discover a rewarding experience beneath its dated exterior.

Rating: 6/10
